raw_question: What care transition interventions reduce 30-day readmission in CHF?

pico.P: Adult patients (≥18 years) hospitalized with a primary diagnosis of heart failure (HFrEF, HFpEF, or HFmrEF) being discharged from an acute care hospital
pico.I: Care transition interventions initiated at or around hospital discharge, including: early outpatient follow-up (cardiology or primary care within 7–14 days), transitional care models (e.g., Bridge to Home, BOOST), nurse-led or pharmacist-led discharge education, remote monitoring or telemonitoring, post-discharge telephone follow-up, home health visits, patient navigator programs, medication reconciliation programs, and multidisciplinary transitional care teams
pico.C: Usual care (standard hospital discharge without a structured care transition program)
O: Time to first post-discharge follow-up appointment
pico.S: Randomized controlled trials, systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and prospective cohort studies; publication year 2000 onward
inclusion_criteria: Adult patients (≥18 years) with heart failure (any ejection fraction)
Hospitalized for acute decompensated heart failure or with heart failure as a primary discharge diagnosis
Intervention initiated at or around hospital discharge (within 7 days of discharge date)
Reports 30-day readmission or closely related readmission outcome as a primary or secondary endpoint
Study design: RCT, systematic review, meta-analysis, or prospective observational study
exclusion_criteria: Interventions initiated >7 days post-discharge (chronic disease management without a transition component)
Studies reporting only inpatient management without a post-discharge follow-up component
Case reports, editorials, letters, narrative commentaries without original data
Populations dominated by post-transplant or LVAD patients where HF management differs fundamentally

fundamental_four.what_we_know: Primary cardiology follow-up after discharge is important for CHF patients, but it is unclear which specific care transition interventions have true evidence of effectiveness.
fundamental_four.what_we_dont_know: Which specific care transition interventions would work best at a given community hospital -- the gap is translating evidence to local implementation priorities.
fundamental_four.what_we_should_know: Which interventions are most effective at reducing 30-day readmission, and how to prioritize them by effectiveness relative to resource requirements and implementation difficulty.
fundamental_four.why_we_should_know: To decrease readmissions in the CHF population -- evidence will drive intervention selection and program development.
